items.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: 385x more efficient inference
items.summary: A new approach to inference using energy-based reasoning has been developed, demonstrating a staggering 385 times efficiency improvement over traditional methods. This advancement could significantly impact AI model deployment and performance optimization for developers and engineers.

items.title: Quad9 Is Leaving France: Why DNS Resolvers Are the Wrong Place to Fight Piracy
items.summary: Quad9's decision to withdraw from France highlights the challenges DNS resolvers face in combating piracy through blocking. This development raises important questions about the role of DNS in internet governance and the implications for privacy and security.

items.title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
items.summary: Recent findings indicate that Google's AI-driven answers are leading to a 40% reduction in search traffic, suggesting a shift in user behavior and expectations. Developers and SEO professionals need to adapt strategies to account for this changing landscape in search engine optimization.

items.title: Harvard researchers find AI coding agents shifted the bottleneck to code review
items.summary: A study from Harvard reveals that the introduction of AI coding agents has shifted the bottleneck in software development from coding to code review processes. This insight is crucial for engineers looking to optimize workflows and improve collaboration in development teams.

items.title: Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64
items.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability has been discovered in OpenJDK related to Base64 processing, posing significant security risks. Developers using OpenJDK must prioritize patching and securing their applications to prevent potential exploits.
